source.note: Captures the OpenAI chat OutboundTransformer.TransformError mapping: an upstream httpclient.Error with StatusCode=400 and JSON body {"error":{"message":"Invalid request","type":"invalid_request_error","code":"invalid_request"}} must produce an llm.ResponseError with StatusCode=400, Detail.Message='Invalid request', Detail.Type='invalid_request_error'. The Go test also asserts Detail.Message and Detail.Type exactly. The 'code' field ('invalid_request') is present in the upstream body but is NOT asserted by the Go test (only message+type are checked) — it is preserved here verbatim from the source fixture but flagged in _comment. The 'nvidia error with numeric code' sibling case in the same Go test demonstrates numeric code coercion (400 instead of string) but is not included as a separate case to keep this file focused. inbound_http, unified_request, selected_channel and outbound_http are null because OutboundTransformer.TransformError does not exercise request stages. client_http is null because this is the OUTBOUND error path (upstream -> unified); the inbound error path (unified -> client) is covered by anthropic/error_inbound_internal.json.

upstream_http._comment: Verbatim from TestOutboundTransformer_TransformError case 'http error with json body'. The Go test constructs httpclient.Error{StatusCode: 400, Body: []byte(`{"error":{"message":"Invalid request","type":"invalid_request_error","code":"invalid_request"}}`)} and feeds it to transformer.TransformError. Status 400 = http.StatusBadRequest.

unified_error._comment: Extension field (NOT one of the six required sections) recording the llm.ResponseError produced by OutboundTransformer.TransformError. The Go test asserts llmErr.StatusCode==400, llmErr.Detail.Message=='Invalid request', llmErr.Detail.Type=='invalid_request_error'. Detail.Code ('invalid_request') is present in the upstream body but is NOT asserted by the Go test for this case (pending source snapshot for whether OutboundTransformer copies code verbatim).
